claim: Dopamine cells in the ventral tegmental area (VTADA) are critical for a variety of motivated behaviors.
source: Dopamine cells in the ventral tegmental area (VTADA) are critical for a variety of motivated behaviors.
evidence: This is a general statement supported by established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: VTADA cells receive synaptic inputs from over 100 anatomically defined brain regions.
source: These cells receive synaptic inputs from over 100 anatomically defined brain regions, which enables control from a distributed set of inputs across the brain.
evidence: This is stated as a known fact about VTA connectivity.

claim: All previous studies mapping inputs to VTA cells have the limitation that inputs local to the VTA cannot be properly assessed due to non-Cre-dependent uptake of EnvA-pseudotyped virus.
source: However, all of these studies have the same fundamental limitation that inputs local to the VTA cannot be properly assessed due to non-Cre-dependent uptake of EnvA-pseudotyped virus.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of previous methodologies.

claim: The quantitative contribution of local inputs to the VTA, including GABAergic, DAergic, and serotonergic, is not known.
source: Therefore, the quantitative contribution of local inputs to the VTA, including GABAergic, DAergic, and serotonergic, is not known.
evidence: This is stated as a gap in current knowledge.

claim: Nearly half of the total inputs to VTADA cells are located locally.
source: I found that nearly half of the total inputs to VTADA cells are located locally, revealing a substantial portion of inputs that have been missed by previous analyses.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the experimental data presented in the study.

claim: The majority of inhibition to VTADA cells arises from the substantia nigra pars reticulata.
source: The majority of inhibition to VTADA cells arises from the substantia nigra pars reticulata, with large contributions from the VTA and the substantia nigra pars compacta.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the experimental data presented in the study.

claim: DA neurons receive inputs from VTAGABA neurons.
source: In addition to receiving inputs from VTAGABA neurons, DA neurons are connected with other DA neurons within the VTA as well as the nearby retrorubal field.
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data presented in the study.

claim: DA neurons are connected with other DA neurons within the VTA as well as the nearby retrorubal field.
source: In addition to receiving inputs from VTAGABA neurons, DA neurons are connected with other DA neurons within the VTA as well as the nearby retrorubal field.
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data presented in the study.

claim: VTADA neurons receive inputs from distributed serotonergic neurons throughout the midbrain and hindbrain.
source: Lastly, I show that VTADA neurons receive inputs from distributed serotonergic neurons throughout the midbrain and hindbrain, with the majority arising from the dorsal raphe.
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data presented in the study.

claim: The majority of serotonergic inputs to VTADA neurons arise from the dorsal raphe.
source: Lastly, I show that VTADA neurons receive inputs from distributed serotonergic neurons throughout the midbrain and hindbrain, with the majority arising from the dorsal raphe.
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data presented in the study.

claim: Ventral tegmental area (VTADA) cells mediate a variety of motivated behaviors, including reward and aversion.
source: Ventral tegmental area (VTADA) cells mediate a variety of motivated behaviors, including reward and aversion (Björklund and Dunnett, 2007; Bromberg-Martin et al., 2010; Cohen et al., 2012; Lammel et al., 2012; Wise, 2004).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: One-step rabies virus (RABV) enables the mapping of inputs onto defined cell types.
source: The recent advent of one-step rabies virus (RABV) has enabled the mapping of inputs onto defined cell types (Wickersham et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: One-step RABV was employed nearly a decade ago to map brain-wide inputs to DA cells in the VTA and the adjacent substantia nigra pars compacta (SNc).
source: This strategy was employed nearly a decade ago to map brain-wide inputs to DA cells in the VTA and the adjacent substantia nigra pars compacta (SNc) (Watabe-Uchida et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: DA neurons in the VTA and SNc are heterogenous in their molecular signatures, projection patterns, physiological properties, and behavioral functions.
source: However, DA neurons in the VTA and SNc are not homogenous, but rather are heterogenous in their molecular signatures, projection patterns, physiological properties, and behavioral functions (Kim et al., 2016; Lammel et al., 2008; Lammel et al., 2011; Lammel et al., 2012; Lerner et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: TRIO (Tracing the Relationship between Inputs and Outputs) was designed to map the input–output relationship of projection-defined VTADA cells.
source: We therefore designed a method, Tracing the Relationship between Inputs and Outputs (TRIO) to map the input–output relationship of projection-defined VTADA cells (Beier et al., 2015; Lerner et al., 2015; Schwarz et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: TRIO revealed that different subtypes of VTADA cells received biased inputs.
source: TRIO revealed that different subtypes of VTADA cells received biased inputs, and that global input–output maps could be used to infer the behavioral contribution of particular input sites, such as the cortex (Beier et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Global input–output maps could be used to infer the behavioral contribution of particular input sites, such as the cortex.
source: TRIO revealed that different subtypes of VTADA cells received biased inputs, and that global input–output maps could be used to infer the behavioral contribution of particular input sites, such as the cortex (Beier et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Each study mapping global inputs to VTADA and SNcDA cells has the same limitation that only inputs located at a distance from the injection site in the midbrain can be assessed.
source: While these and more recent studies have mapped global inputs to VTADA and SNcDA cells (Beier et al., 2015; Faget et al., 2016; Lerner et al., 2015; Menegas et al., 2015; Watabe-Uchida et al., 2012) each study has the same limitation that only inputs located at a distance from the injection site in the midbrain can be assessed.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of previous studies with citations.

claim: The Cre-dependent TVA protein that facilitates EnvA-mediated infection is also expressed at low levels in non-Cre-expressing cells near the site of injection.
source: This is because the Cre-dependent TVA protein that facilitates EnvA-mediated infection is also expressed at low levels in non-Cre-expressing cells near the site of injection (Miyamichi et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: RABV virions that are pseudotyped with the EnvA protein can infect both Cre-expressing starter cells and non-Cre-expressing cells nearby that express low levels of TVA through leaky, non-Cre-dependent expression.
source: Therefore, RABV virions that are pseudotyped with the EnvA protein can infect both Cre-expressing starter cells and non-Cre-expressing cells nearby that express low levels of TVA through leaky, non-Cre-dependent expression.
evidence: This is an inference based on the previous statement about TVA expression.

claim: Leaky gene expression is due to incomplete suppression of transcription/translation of TVA.
source: This leaky gene expression is due to incomplete suppression of transcription/translation of TVA.
evidence: This is stated as an explanation for the observed phenomenon.

claim: Only a single functional unit – presumably three TVA molecules bound to an EnvA trimer – is required to enable infection of EnvA-pseudotyped RABV.
source: Only a single functional unit – presumably three TVA molecules bound to an EnvA trimer (Alsteens et al., 2017) – is required to enable infection of EnvA-pseudotyped RABV.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Injection of AAVs expressing TVA and RABV-G 2 weeks prior to injection of EnvA-pseudotyped RABV can result in thousands of infection events near the injection site, even in Cre− animals that should not express TVA.
source: Injection of adeno-associated viruses (AAVs) expressing TVA and RABV-G 2 weeks prior to injection of EnvA-pseudotyped RABV can result in thousands of infection events near the injection site, even in Cre− animals that should not express TVA (Beier et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: These infections do not occur if AAVs are not injected, demonstrating that the off-target labeling is TVA-mediated.
source: Notably, these infections do not occur if AAVs are not injected, demonstrating that the off-target labeling is TVA-mediated.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from control experiments.

claim: A mutant version of TVA with a single-point mutation (Glu66 → Thr, or TC66T) exhibits only 10% of the efficiency of the wild-type TVA.
source: A mutant version of TVA with a single-point mutation (Glu66 → Thr, or TC66T) that exhibits only 10% of the efficiency of the wild-type TVA dramatically reduces local off-target labeling (Miyamichi et al., 2013; Rong et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: TC66T dramatically reduces local off-target labeling.
source: A mutant version of TVA with a single-point mutation (Glu66 → Thr, or TC66T) that exhibits only 10% of the efficiency of the wild-type TVA dramatically reduces local off-target labeling (Miyamichi et al., 2013; Rong et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Using TC66T enables analysis of the quantitative contribution of local inputs to defined cell types, such as VTADA neurons.
source: Using this variant enables analysis of the quantitative contribution of local inputs to defined cell types, such as VTADA neurons.
evidence: This is stated as a methodological advantage.

claim: Almost half of the inputs to VTADA cells are located near the VTA.
source: I used the TC66T variant in place of the wild-type TVA, TCB, in my tracing studies and found that almost half of the inputs to VTADA cells are located near the VTA; many of these represent inputs that were missed or may have been misquantified in the previous studies.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the experimental data presented in the study.

claim: Many local inputs to VTADA cells represent inputs that were missed or may have been misquantified in previous studies.
source: I used the TC66T variant in place of the wild-type TVA, TCB, in my tracing studies and found that almost half of the inputs to VTADA cells are located near the VTA; many of these represent inputs that were missed or may have been misquantified in the previous studies.
evidence: This is an inference based on the comparison with previous studies.

claim: Between 900 and 2,400 starter cells were observed in experiments performed in DAT-Cre mice.
source: When experiments were performed in DAT-Cre mice, between 900 and 2,400 starter cells were observed, and an average of 23,000 total input cells were labeled per experiment (Figure 1B, C).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experimental data.

claim: An average of 23,000 total input cells were labeled per experiment in DAT-Cre mice.
source: When experiments were performed in DAT-Cre mice, between 900 and 2,400 starter cells were observed, and an average of 23,000 total input cells were labeled per experiment (Figure 1B, C).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experimental data.

claim: The majority of starter cells were located within the parabrachial pigmented nucleus (PBP: 58% ± 6%) and paranigral nucleus (PN: 27% ± 6%) of the VTA.
source: The majority of starter cells were located within the parabrachial pigmented nucleus (PBP: 58% ± 6%) and paranigral nucleus (PN: 27% ± 6%) of the VTA.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experimental data.

claim: 8% ± 3% of starter neurons were located within the medial aspect of the SNc.
source: The rest of the starter neurons were located within the medial aspect of the SNc (8% ± 3%), interfascicular nucleus of the VTA (IF: 5% ± 2%), and rostrolinear nucleus (Rli: 2% ± 1%).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experimental data.

claim: 5% ± 2% of starter neurons were located in the interfascicular nucleus of the VTA (IF).
source: The rest of the starter neurons were located within the medial aspect of the SNc (8% ± 3%), interfascicular nucleus of the VTA (IF: 5% ± 2%), and rostrolinear nucleus (Rli: 2% ± 1%).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experimental data.

claim: 2% ± 1% of starter neurons were located in the rostrolinear nucleus (Rli).
source: The rest of the starter neurons were located within the medial aspect of the SNc (8% ± 3%), interfascicular nucleus of the VTA (IF: 5% ± 2%), and rostrolinear nucleus (Rli: 2% ± 1%).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experimental data.

claim: DA neurons projecting to the medial prefrontal cortex and medial shell of the nucleus accumbens are mostly located in the PN, IF, and medial PBP.
source: For example, DA neurons projecting to the medial prefrontal cortex and medial shell of the nucleus accumbens are mostly located in the PN, IF, and medial PBP; those projecting to the amygdala are interspersed throughout the PBP; and those projecting to the lateral shell of the nucleus accumbens are largely located in the lateral PBP (Lammel et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: DA neurons projecting to the amygdala are interspersed throughout the PBP.
source: For example, DA neurons projecting to the medial prefrontal cortex and medial shell of the nucleus accumbens are mostly located in the PN, IF, and medial PBP; those projecting to the amygdala are interspersed throughout the PBP; and those projecting to the lateral shell of the nucleus accumbens are largely located in the lateral PBP (Lammel et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: DA neurons projecting to the lateral shell of the nucleus accumbens are largely located in the lateral PBP.
source: For example, DA neurons projecting to the medial prefrontal cortex and medial shell of the nucleus accumbens are mostly located in the PN, IF, and medial PBP; those projecting to the amygdala are interspersed throughout the PBP; and those projecting to the lateral shell of the nucleus accumbens are largely located in the lateral PBP (Lammel et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The number of RABV-labeled inputs scaled with the number of starter cells.
source: The number of RABV-labeled inputs scaled with the number of starter cells, as expected (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is a result from the experimental data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: The average convergence index using TC66T was approximately 8.
source: The average convergence index using TC66T was approximately 8, which was not significantly different from tracing performed using TCB (Figure 1H).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experimental data shown in Figure 1H.

claim: The convergence index using TC66T was not significantly different from tracing performed using TCB.
source: The average convergence index using TC66T was approximately 8, which was not significantly different from tracing performed using TCB (Figure 1H).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the experimental data shown in Figure 1H.

claim: The convergence index using TC66T was similar to the convergence index of 7 reported by Watabe-Uchida et al. using a nonmutated TVA.
source: Notably, this was also similar to the convergence index of 7 reported by the study from Watabe-Uchida et al. using a nonmutated TVA that reported only a small number of inputs local to the VTA (Watabe-Uchida et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a comparison with a previous study supported by a citation.

claim: 46% of the inputs to VTADA cells arose from local regions that were not quantified in previous analysis.
source: However, in my study nearly half (46%) of the inputs to VTADA cells arose from local regions that were not quantified in my previous analysis.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experimental data.

claim: Faget et al. excluded the VTA, SNc, substantia nigra pars reticulata (SNr), red nucleus (RPC), and interpeduncular nucleus (IPN) from their analysis.
source: Though Faget et al. excluded the VTA, SNc, substantia nigra pars reticulata (SNr), red nucleus (RPC), and interpeduncular nucleus (IPN) likely for precisely the reason that concerned us, these regions combined to yield 20% of the total inputs to the VTA.
evidence: This is stated as a comparison with a previous study.

claim: The VTA, SNc, SNr, RPC, and IPN combined to yield 20% of the total inputs to the VTA.
source: Though Faget et al. excluded the VTA, SNc, substantia nigra pars reticulata (SNr), red nucleus (RPC), and interpeduncular nucleus (IPN) likely for precisely the reason that concerned us, these regions combined to yield 20% of the total inputs to the VTA.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experimental data.

claim: About 10% of the total inputs are within the VTA itself.
source: This included about 10% of the total inputs within the VTA itself, 6% in the adjacent substantia nigra, and 4% in other nearby regions.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experimental data.

claim: 6% of the total inputs are in the adjacent substantia nigra.
source: This included about 10% of the total inputs within the VTA itself, 6% in the adjacent substantia nigra, and 4% in other nearby regions.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experimental data.

claim: 4% of the total inputs are in other nearby regions.
source: This included about 10% of the total inputs within the VTA itself, 6% in the adjacent substantia nigra, and 4% in other nearby regions.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experimental data.

claim: Data from the current study mixed with that from the Faget et al. study for long-range inputs.
source: Using dimensional reduction techniques such as Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP) to compare the overall labeling patterns within these three groups, I found that my data mixed with that from the Faget et al. study for long-range inputs (comparison 3) suggesting that the data were comparable.
evidence: This is a result from the UMAP analysis comparing datasets.

claim: Data from the two studies segregated for both the excluded and questionable brain regions.
source: However, data from the two studies segregated for both the excluded (comparison 1) and questionable (comparison 2) brain regions (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a result from the UMAP analysis comparing datasets shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Data mixing in UMAP space supports the conclusion that the variances between the datasets are similar, and thus the datasets can be compared.
source: Data mixing in UMAP space supports the conclusion that the variances between the datasets are similar, and thus the datasets can be compared.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the UMAP analysis results.

claim: Separation of the two datasets in UMAP space suggests that these datasets cannot be readily compared as the variances between input sites in the datasets are different.
source: In contrast, separation of the two datasets in UMAP space suggests that these datasets cannot be readily compared as the variances between input sites in the datasets are different.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the UMAP analysis results.

claim: The method of using a modified, less efficient version of TVA is necessary to properly examine the local input landscape in the ventral midbrain.
source: These results support the likelihood that the method of using a modified, less efficient version of TVA is necessary to properly examine the local input landscape in the ventral midbrain.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the comparison of datasets.

claim: Long-range inputs to DA neurons measured using RABV tracing have been published several times.
source: Long-range inputs to DA neurons measured using RABV tracing have been published several times (Beier et al., 2015; Faget et al., 2016; Watabe-Uchida et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: DA neurons have been subdivided by output site, and the inputs to particular subpopulations compared to one another.
source: More recently, DA neurons have been subdivided by output site, and the inputs to particular subpopulations compared to one another (Beier et al., 2015; Beier et al., 2019; Derdeyn et al., 2021; Lammel et al., 2012; Menegas et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: These analyses have enabled understanding of how input patterns relate to one another, and which inputs are biased onto which sets of VTADA cells.
source: These analyses have enabled us to understand how input patterns relate to one another, and which inputs are biased onto which sets of VTADA cells.
evidence: This is stated as a benefit of previous analyses.

claim: Much less is known about the patterns of innervation from local inputs.
source: However, much less is known about the patterns of innervation from local inputs.
evidence: This is stated as a gap in current knowledge.

claim: Local input sites intermingled with long-distance inputs in UMAP analysis.
source: I found that local input sites intermingled with long-distance inputs (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a result from the UMAP analysis shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Local inputs co-organize with long-distance inputs, rather than being a separate set of circuits.
source: This is expected, and suggests that local inputs co-organize with long-distance inputs, rather than being a separate set of circuits.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the UMAP analysis results.

claim: The region associations in the UMAP analysis were robust, with only three long-range input regions associating with different groups of inputs across conditions.
source: I found that the region associations were robust, with only three long-range input regions – the nucleus accumbens medial shell (NAcMed), nucleus accumbens core (NAcCore), and extended amygdala (EAM) associating with different groups of inputs across conditions (Figure 2B, C).
evidence: This is a result from the UMAP analysis shown in Figure 2B, C.

claim: Three clusters of input regions were observed in the UMAP analysis.
source: Similar to my 76 brain dataset, I observed three clusters of input regions (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is a result from the UMAP analysis shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The first cluster is the set of brain regions that predominately project lateral or dorsal to the VTA.
source: The first is the set of brain regions that predominately project lateral or dorsal to the VTA (Derdeyn et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a characterization of one of the UMAP clusters supported by a citation.

claim: Regions that project laterally include inputs from the basal ganglia such as the dorsal striatum (DStr), nucleus accumbens lateral shell (NAcLat), globus pallidus external segment (GPe), and cortex.
source: The regions that project laterally include inputs from the basal ganglia such as the dorsal striatum (DStr), nucleus accumbens lateral shell (NAcLat), globus pallidus external segment (GPe), and cortex.
evidence: This is a characterization of regions in the first UMAP cluster.

claim: Regions that project dorsally include the entopeduncular nucleus (EP), zona incerta (ZI), and deep cerebellar nuclei (DCN).
source: Those that project dorsally include the entopeduncular nucleus (EP), zona incerta (ZI), and deep cerebellar nuclei (DCN).
evidence: This is a characterization of regions in the first UMAP cluster.

claim: The local inputs that associate with cluster 1 include mostly those located dorsally and laterally to the VTA, including the periaqueductal gray (PAG), midbrain reticular nucleus (mRT), interstitial nucleus of Cajal (InC), subpeduncular tegmental nucleus (SPTg), subbrachial nucleus (SubB), SNr, and substantia nigra pars lateralis (SNl).
source: The local inputs that associate with this cluster include mostly those located dorsally and laterally to the VTA, including the periaqueductal gray (PAG), midbrain reticular nucleus (mRT), interstitial nucleus of Cajal (InC), subpeduncular tegmental nucleus (SPTg), subbrachial nucleus (SubB), SNr, and substantia nigra pars lateralis (SNl).
evidence: This is a characterization of local inputs in the first UMAP cluster.

claim: Three selected inputs in cluster 1 – the SNr, mRT, and PAG – displayed a lateral bias in the VTA.
source: I indeed observed that three selected inputs in cluster 1 – the SNr, mRT, and PAG – displayed a lateral bias in the VTA (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a result from the analysis of Allen Mouse Brain Connectivity Atlas data shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The second cluster of inputs includes mostly regions that project uniformly across the VTA, including the lateral hypothalamus (LH), paraventricular hypothalamus (PVH), and bed nucleus of the stria terminalis (BNST).
source: The second cluster of inputs includes mostly regions that project uniformly across the VTA, including the lateral hypothalamus (LH), paraventricular hypothalamus (PVH), and bed nucleus of the stria terminalis (BNST) (Derdeyn et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a characterization of the second UMAP cluster supported by a citation.

claim: The local inputs associating with cluster 2 include inputs from all of the subregions of the VTA itself (PBP, PN, and IF), and other inputs located along the midline [median raphe (MnR), supramammillary decussation (SuMx), medial mammillary nucleus (MM)] as well as those located just laterally to the midline such as the red nucleus (RPC), ventral tegmental nucleus (VTg), inferior colliculus (IC), and parasubthalamic nucleus (PSth).
source: The local inputs associating with this cluster include inputs from all of the subregions of the VTA itself (PBP, PN, and IF), and other inputs located along the midline [median raphe (MnR), supramammillary decussation (SuMx), medial mammillary nucleus (MM)] as well as those located just laterally to the midline such as the red nucleus (RPC), ventral tegmental nucleus (VTg), inferior colliculus (IC), and parasubthalamic nucleus (PSth).
evidence: This is a characterization of local inputs in the second UMAP cluster.

claim: The PSth, RPC, and IC show a more consistent projection across the medial–lateral axis of the VTA.
source: While more varied in their individual projections, the PSth, RPC, and IC show a more consistent projection across the medial–lateral axis of the VTA (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a result from the analysis of Allen Mouse Brain Connectivity Atlas data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The final cluster of inputs mostly includes those that project medially within the VTA.
source: The final cluster of inputs mostly includes those that project medially within the VTA.
evidence: This is a characterization of the third UMAP cluster.

claim: The third cluster includes the medial habenula (MHb) and lateral habenula (LHb), septum, preoptic nucleus (PO), and laterodorsal tegmentum (LDT).
source: This includes the medial habenula (MHb) and lateral habenula (LHb), septum, preoptic nucleus (PO), and laterodorsal tegmentum (LDT).
evidence: This is a characterization of regions in the third UMAP cluster.

claim: Local inputs associating with cluster 3 include midline structures such as the interpeduncular nucleus (IPN), raphe magnus (RMg), supramammillary nucleus (SuM), structures near the midline such as the reticulotegmental nucleus (RtTg), anterior tegmental nucleus (ATg), superior colliculus (SC), slightly more lateral structures such as the retrorubal field (RRF) and pedunculopontine tegmental nucleus (PPTg), or inputs with lower counts such as the microcellular tegmental nucleus (MiTg) and the dorsal nucleus of the lateral lemniscus (DLL).
source: Local inputs associating with this group include midline structures such as the interpeduncular nucleus (IPN), raphe magnus (RMg), supramammillary nucleus (SuM), structures near the midline such as the reticulotegmental nucleus (RtTg), anterior tegmental nucleus (ATg), superior colliculus (SC), slightly more lateral structures such as the retrorubal field (RRF) and pedunculopontine tegmental nucleus (PPTg), or inputs with lower counts such as the microcellular tegmental nucleus (MiTg) and the dorsal nucleus of the lateral lemniscus (DLL).
evidence: This is a characterization of local inputs in the third UMAP cluster.

claim: The IPN, SuM, and SC all showed a medial bias in the VTA.
source: The IPN, SuM, and SC all showed a medial bias in the VTA (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is a result from the analysis of Allen Mouse Brain Connectivity Atlas data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The difference in medial–lateral preference among the three clusters was especially clear when averaged across the three tested regions and plotted together.
source: The difference in medial–lateral preference among the three clusters was especially clear when averaged across the three tested regions and plotted together (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is a result from the analysis shown in Figure 3E.

claim: There is a topographical organization of inputs to the VTA that applies to both long-distance and local inputs, whereby inputs segregate based on their projection medially or laterally within the VTA.
source: These data in sum suggest a topographical organization of inputs to the VTA that applies to both long-distance and local inputs, whereby inputs segregate based on their projection medially or laterally within the VTA, as we have found previously with long-range inputs (Beier et al., 2015; Beier et al., 2019; Derdeyn et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data, supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The majority of studies of inhibition to VTADA cells have focused on either GABA neurons within the VTA or on the rostromedial tegmental nucleus (RMTg).
source: The majority of studies of inhibition to VTADA cells have focused on either GABA neurons within the VTA or on an anatomically poorly defined structure referred to as the rostromedial tegmental nucleus (RMTg) (Jhou, 2005; Jhou et al., 2009a; Jhou et al., 2009b; Kaufling et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Optogenetic stimulation of local GABAergic cells in the VTA inhibits DA cells and is aversive.
source: For example, optogenetic stimulation of local GABAergic cells in the VTA inhibits DA cells and is aversive (Bouarab et al., 2019; Tan et al., 2012; van Zessen et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: GABAergic populations in the VTA are likely heterogenous, as they receive differential innervation from input structures and differentially influence different sets of DA cells.
source: These GABAergic populations are likely heterogenous, as they receive differential innervation from input structures and differentially influence different sets of DA cells (Yang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: DA neurons located more laterally in the VTA received a stronger spontaneous inhibitory input than DA cells located more medially.
source: Notably, DA neurons located more laterally in the VTA received a stronger spontaneous inhibitory input than DA cells located more medially (Yang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The likelihood of a DA cell being inhibited by an aversive stimulus related to the location of the dendrites of those cells, which influenced the number of GABAergic synapses these cells received.
source: Furthermore, the likelihood of a DA cell being inhibited by an aversive stimulus related to the location of the dendrites of those cells, which influenced the number of GABAergic synapses these cells received (Henny et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The GABAergic synapse density was higher for dendrites located in the SNr than the SNc.
source: Notably, the GABAergic synapse density was higher for dendrites located in the SNr than the SNc, indicating that the location of connections in the ventral midbrain influenced the probability of whether they were excitatory or inhibitory.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from previous research.

claim: The majority of starter neurons in the GABAergic input mapping experiments were located within the PBP nucleus of the VTA (63% ± 1%).
source: The majority of starter neurons were located within the PBP nucleus of the VTA (63% ± 1%), followed by VTA PN (15% ± 1%), SNc (11% ± 2%), VTA IF (6% ± 1%), and Rli (3% ± 1%).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experimental data.

claim: The SNr is the single largest source of inhibition onto VTADA cells, representing 20.1% ± 1.4% of all inhibitory inputs.
source: I found that, surprisingly, the SNr is the single largest source of inhibition onto the cells that I targeted, representing 20.1% ± 1.4% of all inhibitory inputs (Figure 4F, G).
